record.paper_title: Recent Progress and Open Problems in Function Field Arithmetic — The Influence of John Tate’s Work
record.context_brief: Fundamental-group background for function-field Ihara theory
record.original_question: What is the correct fundamental-group framework, over function fields, that explains the analogues of Ihara power series, Deligne-Soulé cocycles, higher circular units, and multizeta values in the same way that the Grothendieck-Ihara program and mixed Tate motives over Q explain these objects for the projective line minus three points?

evidence.quote: Ihara power series occurs in Grothendieck-Ihara program of the study of absolute Galois group over Q by realizing it in the automorphism group of the algebraic fundamental group of the projective line minus three points. ... We have these ingredients, as we have the mixed Tate-motives theory in function fields, but we have no good understanding of the fundamental group background yet!

artifact.category_tag: Function field arithmetic and motivic fundamental groups
artifact.status_search_result: Surveys and recent papers (Thakur's multizeta survey, work of Anderson–Thakur, Chang and others on mixed Carlitz–Tate t-motives) develop the period/t-motive side and partial Galois cocycle constructions, but no fundamental-group framework over function fields has been established that simultaneously explains Ihara power series, Deligne–Soulé cocycles, higher cyclotomic units, and multizeta values in the way the Grothendieck–Ihara program does over Q. The question appears to remain open as of the most recent literature.

status_evidence.title: Multizeta values for function fields: A survey (Thakur)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses function-field multizeta values, their period interpretations via mixed Carlitz–Tate t-motives, and connections to the Grothendieck–Ihara program; identifies the missing fundamental-group framework.
status_evidence.claim: The fundamental-group analogue is acknowledged as not yet established, while period and cocycle pieces exist.

status_evidence.title: Grothendieck–Teichmüller Theory, Moduli Spaces and Multizeta Values (Schneps notes)
status_evidence.snippet: Reviews the classical Grothendieck–Ihara picture over Q via π_1 of P^1 minus three points and motivic multizeta values.
status_evidence.claim: Provides the Q-side framework whose function-field analogue is sought.
